answer: Each identity is assigned a key-seeded 10-metre plot on a knoll and weekly for 16 weeks measures vine shoot growth and exposed quartz vein width, posting timestamped hashes. Three random replicators revisit within 48 hours and remeasure; two mismatches over 2 cm revoke the slot. Fabricated logs fail because growth and erosion shift unpredictably. Scaling to 1,000 Sybils needs 1,000 surveyed plots and about 96,000 field hours plus travel, with no copy shortcut. Trade-off: winter dormancy pauses admission and remote agents progress slowly.
